_comment: REAL EXCAVATION DATA. Companion to t111-2025-layout.json and
`description` and `catalog` come from the season's Special Finds List;
`gridX`, `gridY`, `elevation` and the tolerances come from the daily log
entry on the page cited. Where the two records disagree, both are kept
and the disagreement is named in _known_problems.
Grid coordinates are signed: South and West negative. The trench book
writes '204.25E/36.75S'; that is (204.25, -36.75) here. Elevations are
metres above sea level on the corrected 29.23 mAE datum.
The Methodology section describes how each one was measured: a plumb bob
over the findspot, a tape run at right angles to two baulk strings for
the coordinates, and a line level from the datum for the elevation.

finds.context_note: Found while cutting the eastern baulk wall, which is worked below the trench floor

finds.description: Architectural terracotta with possible score marks (3 associated fragments)

list.columns: SF#, Date, Pg#, Locus, Description, Cataloged?, Catalog #

coordinates.record: T111, 2025, NKD V Trench Book, daily log entries
note: Every one of the 26 has a coordinate and an elevation in the log.
Only SF 1, 2 and 3 carry stated tolerances, because only those three
were recovered from the wheelbarrow rather than in situ: their
coordinate is where the bucket came from, not where the object lay.

method.record: T111, 2025, NKD V Trench Book, Methodology section
note: 'a plumb bob will be held over the location of the special find, and
the distance from two of the perpendicular baulk walls will be
determined by extending a tape measure at a right angle ... a string
with a line level will be attached to a fixed datum point'. The
Methodology quotes the datum as 29.23 mAE, the corrected value.

_known_problems: SF 8 AND SF 9 PLOT OUTSIDE THE TRENCH. T111 runs 204E to 209E. SF 8 is at
203.48E, 0.52 m west of the west baulk; SF 9 is at 203.18E, 0.82 m west of
it. Both are recorded as Locus 2, which exists only inside the trench.
Their northings, 32.45S and 33.01S, are in range, and both were found in
the northwest quadrant, so the eastings look like the error.
SF 16 PLOTS OUTSIDE THE SOUNDING AND BELOW IT. The Locus 6 sounding runs
207E-208E by 34S-36S and its floor at closing is 27.74-27.79 mAE. SF 16 is
recorded at 207.30E/33.21S -- 0.79 m north of the sounding -- and at 27.44
mAE, 0.30 m below the deepest point the sounding ever reached, and below
the surface of unexcavated Locus 8. The daily log places it 'in the
northern meter of the sounding'. Both numbers contradict the prose.
SF 17 PLOTS 0.45 m WEST OF THE SOUNDING, at 206.55E against a west edge of
207E, though its elevation of 27.76 mAE sits correctly within Locus 6.
SF 3'S ELEVATION IS 0.29 m BELOW THE LOCUS. At 27.75 mAE it is below every
Locus 1 closing reading. It was recorded on 1 July with SF 1 (28.56) and
SF 2 (28.35) from the same wheelbarrow at the same nominal spot, on a day
spent lowering a spoil heap whose crest was at 28.70. Nothing on site was
at 27.75 mAE that day.
SF 20 AND SF 21 ARE MARKED 'Cataloged? No' AND GIVEN CATALOGUE NUMBERS
(PC 20250145, PC 20250146) in the same rows. The season conclusion refers
to both numbers as catalogued objects, so the flag is wrong, not the
numbers.
SF 16 IS MARKED 'Cataloged? No' WITH NO NUMBER on the list, but the Locus
6 form and description both give PC 20250126. The number is used here.
SF 20 AND SF 21 ARE 'frieze plaque fragments' on the list and in the daily
log, and 'sima cavetto fragments' in the season conclusion. Two different
architectural terracotta types for the same two catalogue numbers.
SF 10 IS A 'Glass shard' on the list and in the daily log, and an obsidian
flake in the Lithics Summary and the Locus 2 description -- where it is
the trench's only lithic. Obsidian is volcanic glass, so this is plausibly
a re-identification during study rather than a contradiction, but no
record says so. If it is glass, the season's lithic count is zero.
SF 11'S DATE DISAGREES BY ONE DAY: 19/07/2025 on the list, and page 111 of
the trench book, which falls inside the entry for Friday 18 July. The 19th
was a Saturday. The log date is used here.
SF 15'S STATED DEPTH DOES NOT REPRODUCE. The log says it lay 'ca. 13 cm
below the surface of the floor'. Interpolating the Locus 6 opening surface
at its coordinates gives about 27.89 mAE, and the find is at 27.82, which
is 7 cm. The Locus 6 description likewise puts the Archaic frieze material
'approximately 15 to 20 cm beneath the floor' while grouping SF 15 with SF
20 and SF 21, which recompute to about 24 cm. Depths quoted in prose and
depths recomputed from the recorded surfaces are not the same numbers.
SF 22 HAS NO LOCUS IN THE DAILY LOG and one decimal place on its elevation
(27.6) where every other reading has two. The list assigns it Locus 7.
